title: Autoscribe Config
description: Committed configuration for an Autoscribe docs site. Lives at `.autoscribe/config.json` in the docs (tenant) repo and travels with the project. Holds NO secrets — the model credential is a GitHub repo secret (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for an API key, or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for a Claude subscription token), never stored here.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor IntelliSense.

watchedRepo.description: The code repository Autoscribe documents and watches for merged PRs, in `owner/name` form. One watched repo per docs site (1:1 for the MVP).

docsDir.description: Directory in THIS docs repo where Docusaurus markdown/MDX content lives. Autoscribe writes and edits files only under this path (plus `sidebars.ts`).

style.description: House-style hints handed to the editorial pass and the per-PR analyst so generated prose is consistent.

voice.description: Desired writing voice / tone for generated docs. Free text — it is handed to the editorial pass as guidance. Two values are recognised specially: `simplified technical english` (or `ASD-STE100`) switches the editorial pass into controlled-language mode, which caps sentence length, requires the imperative for instructions, bans the passive voice, and applies STE word substitutions; anything else is treated as ordinary tone guidance on top of the default house style.

audience.description: Primary reader the docs are written for. Steers depth and vocabulary.

model.description: Claude model alias used for per-PR sync work (the common, cost-sensitive path). Sonnet is the conservative default.

initModel.description: Claude model alias used only for the one-time initial full-repo build (`autoscribe-init`), where extra capability is worth the cost.

maxTurns.description: Hard cap on agent turns for a single run, passed to the runtime as `--max-turns`. This is the cost control the workflows actually enforce: the agent is cut off once it hits the cap, whatever it has spent. Defaults differ by workflow — the per-PR sync uses 40, the one-time initial build uses 200 — so leave this unset unless you have a reason to override both.

waveSize.description: Maximum number of parallel sub-agents per wave during fan-out (e.g. the initial build's one-section-per-agent pass). Caps concurrency to keep cost and rate-limit pressure predictable. Ported from the reference pipeline's wave-based concurrency guard.

spendCeilingUSD.description: Soft spend ceiling, in USD, for a single Action run. When the runner's estimated/observed spend for a run would exceed this, it stops early and records the breach instead of continuing. Because it is the user's own Anthropic key, this is a guardrail against runaway bills. Applies only to `agent.auth: "api_key"` (metered billing); a Claude subscription token is not per-token billed, so this is ignored under `"subscription"` and the agent's own subscription rate limits apply instead.

agent.description: Which agent runtime runs in CI and how it authenticates to the model provider. Holds NO secret — the credential value is a GitHub Actions repo secret, never stored here.

runtime.description: The coding-agent CLI the workflows install and invoke to read the code and write the docs. `claude-code` (Anthropic's @anthropic-ai/claude-code) is the built-in, fully-supported runtime, talking to Anthropic's API. `gateway` runs that same built-in runtime against an Anthropic-compatible endpoint you host instead — a local or self-hosted model behind LiteLLM, claude-code-router, vLLM, or a cloud gateway — configured with `agent.baseUrl`; you keep the whole proven agent loop and only swap where the tokens come from. `custom` is the bring-your-own-agent runtime: the workflow runs `agent.command` (any CLI — openclaw, nanoclaw, your own script) with the task in $AUTOSCRIBE_PROMPT and the standard paths, and the command brings its own model credential. Any other value fails the run with a clear error rather than silently mis-running.

baseUrl.description: Required when `runtime` is `gateway`: the base URL of an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, passed to the built-in runtime as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. The endpoint must speak Anthropic's Messages API — a proxy such as LiteLLM, claude-code-router, or Bifrost puts that shape in front of Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenAI-compatible servers, and most hosted providers. IMPORTANT: the URL is resolved from the GitHub Actions runner, not from your laptop. A GitHub-hosted runner cannot reach `localhost` or a private LAN address — for a truly local model, either run a self-hosted runner on the same network or expose the endpoint through a tunnel. Ignored unless `runtime` is `gateway`.

command.description: Required when `runtime` is `custom`: the shell command that runs your own agent. It runs with NO GitHub token in scope (same sandbox as the built-in runtime) and receives the task via $AUTOSCRIBE_PROMPT / $AUTOSCRIBE_PROMPT_FILE plus $AUTOSCRIBE_WATCHED_PATH (read-only source), $AUTOSCRIBE_DOCS_DIR (where to write docs), and $AUTOSCRIBE_MODEL. Provide whatever model credential your agent needs as a separate GitHub Actions repo secret. Ignored unless `runtime` is `custom`.

auth.description: How the runtime authenticates. `api_key` uses the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repo secret (metered, pay-per-token). `subscription` uses the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN repo secret — a Claude Pro/Max subscription token from `claude setup-token` — billed against the subscription instead of the API, subject to its rate limits. `gateway` uses the AUTOSCRIBE_GATEWAY_TOKEN repo secret as a bearer token for your `agent.baseUrl` endpoint, and is the only value allowed when `runtime` is `gateway`; leave that secret unset if your endpoint needs no credential (common for a model on your own network). Ignored when `runtime` is `custom` (your command manages its own auth).
